## Variable definitions

### infection

`final.diagnosis.1` was used to derive the infection status variables begining with `infect`.

`infect.fct` and `infect.num` are identical 3-level variables, except
the first is formatted as factor while the second is formatted as numeric.

The levels of these variables are defined as follows:

1. Control: `final.diagnosis.1`= "SPE" 
2. Inter: `final.diagnosis.1` = "CPPE"
3. Case: `final.diagnosis.1`= "utrue" or `final.diagnosis.1`= "bacterial"

`infect.bi` is just the cases from above i.e. `infect.num` >2

`infect.bi.new` is `infect.bi` with 
N= `r sum(sign(pheno$infect.bi.new==0), na.rm=T) - sum(sign(pheno$infect.bi==0), na.rm=T)` 
additional controls included who had `final.diagnosis.1` values equal to 
"X/renal/u", "X/hepatic/u", or "X/cardiac/u". 

### comp out

`comp.out` is a variable I received with the title: "composite.outcome..lytics..surgery.or..3m.mortality"



# Protein-wide associations

Phenotypic characteristics of participants described in [Phenotype information](#phenotype-information) were examined for association with protein abundances ([Protein measurements](#protein-measurements))

## Models

The formulae of linear models examined are shown in the table below:

```{r models}
```


## Count of significant hits

Number of significant hits identified per model. Statistical significance was determined using a Bonferroni multiple testing threshold correcting for `r nrow(ret$pleural.infect.fct$ret$table)` tests. That is $$0.05/`r nrow(ret$pleural.infect.fct$ret$table)` = `r sprintf("%.2e",0.05/nrow(ret$pleural.infect.fct$ret$table))`$$

```{r hits}
```
